claims.explanation: Tyrphostin-AG-99 is an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor, and its selectivity is best explained by dependence on EGFR signaling. Sensitive lines include those with EGFR mutations (e.g., HCC4006) or high EGFR expression, while resistant lines often have mutations in downstream effectors (KRAS, BRAF, PTEN, NF1) that bypass EGFR inhibition. Additional sensitivity may arise from co-occurring mutations in PI3K pathway or chromatin modifiers, but the dominant feature is EGFR dependency.

features.basis: Activating EGFR mutations predict response to EGFR inhibitors; HCC4006 is EGFR-mutant and sensitive.
High EGFR expression increases dependence on EGFR signaling, enhancing sensitivity to EGFR inhibitors.
KRAS mutations activate downstream MAPK signaling, bypassing EGFR inhibition; many resistant lines harbor KRAS mutations.
BRAF mutations activate MAPK pathway downstream of EGFR, conferring resistance to EGFR inhibitors.
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT signaling independent of EGFR, reducing sensitivity to EGFR inhibition.
NF1 loss leads to RAS activation, bypassing EGFR dependence.
PIK3CA mutations activate PI3K pathway downstream of EGFR, potentially reducing sensitivity.
ARID1A mutations are enriched in sensitive lines and may confer sensitivity to kinase inhibitors via chromatin remodeling effects.
TP53 mutations are common in sensitive lines, possibly indicating a context that favors EGFR inhibitor response.
NFE2L2 mutations appear in some sensitive lines, potentially linking oxidative stress response to drug sensitivity.
STK11 mutations are present in several sensitive lines, though the mechanism is unclear.
ATM mutations are more frequent in resistant lines, possibly indicating a role in DNA damage response and drug resistance.
